question: A warehouse had 64 pallets of canned beans, tracked over 120 minutes, or 2 hours, of unloading, even though the warehouse has 30 loading docks. A matching shipment doubled the pallet count. Three more matching shipments made it four times as large. A big outbound order removed 314 pallets. A second order removed 142 more. Finally, 16 more pallets were removed for a donation drive. How many pallets were left in the warehouse?

In the morning, Camille's charity bake sale had raised $235. By midday, $22 more came in. In the afternoon, $14 more came in from a raffle. By evening, $68 more came in from a matching donor. Finally, two more matching bake sales across town tripled the total, far more than her rival fundraiser run by Priya, which only made $600. How much money did Camille's bake sale raise in total?

In the morning, a factory had 131 units of a product ready, even though the factory has 20 assembly lines. By midday, 14 more units were produced. In the afternoon, six more matching production runs made the total seven times as large. Later, 78 more units were produced. By evening, six more matching runs made the total seven times as large again. Finally, 2,124 units were shipped out, and a late order made the remaining units five times as large. How many units did the factory have at the end?

A charity had $100 in donations, tallied over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of the fundraiser, even though a dozen volunteers helped run it. A matching donation tripled the total. Five more matching donations made it six times as large. A late gift added $72. Finally, $834 was spent on event costs. How much money did the charity have left?

Two rival food banks compared their canned goods. Westside Food Bank had 136 cans, even though the bank has 15 volunteers. A donation drive added 80 more cans. A second drive added 10 more. Seven more matching drives joined, making the total eight times as large. A late donation added 33 more cans. Finally, a matching partner bank doubled the total, leaving Westside far ahead of the rival Eastside Food Bank's 900 cans. How many cans did Westside Food Bank end up with?

Two neighbors compared their firewood stacks, even though the neighborhood has a dozen houses. Priti had 84 logs stacked. A delivery added 35 more logs. A cold snap used up 85 logs. A second cold snap used up 31 more. Finally, 2 more logs were used for a small fire, leaving her with fewer logs than her neighbor Hugo. How many logs did Priti have left?

In the morning, a bakery had 85 croissants ready. By midday, 10 were sold to early customers. In the afternoon, 33 more were sold during the lunch rush. Later, 24 more were sold to a catering order. By evening, the remaining croissants were split evenly across 3 trays, and only one tray was kept out, and finally 26 more croissants came out of a late oven batch. How many croissants were on that tray by the end of the day?

A warehouse had 224 bicycles in stock, tracked over 120 minutes, or 2 hours, of inventory, even though the warehouse has 15 loading bays. A shipment removed 80 bikes for a big order. A delivery added 76 more bikes. Five more matching shipments made the total six times as large. Finally, 907 bikes were shipped out to stores. How many bicycles were left in the warehouse?

In the morning, a bakery had 173 loaves of bread ready. By midday, seven more matching batches made the total eight times as large. In the afternoon, 43 more loaves came out of a late batch. Later, 52 more loaves were baked. Still later, 38 more loaves came out. By evening, 4 more loaves were added from a small batch. Finally, 40 more loaves came out of the last oven run. How many loaves of bread did the bakery have by the end of the day?

In the morning, a movie theater had 205 seats reserved. By midday, five more matching showings made the total six times as large. In the afternoon, the reservations were split evenly across 6 screens, and only one screen's reservations were counted going forward. By evening, 199 reservations were canceled. Finally, 20 more reservations came in for a late show. How many reservations did that screen have by the end of the day?

A factory produced 128 gears in the first run, even though the factory has 10 machines. Five more matching runs made the total six times as large. Six more matching runs made it seven times as large. The gears were then split evenly across 3 shipping crates, and only one crate's gears were counted. Finally, 1,375 gears were shipped out from that crate. How many gears were left in that crate?

In the morning, a stadium had sold 190 tickets, even though the stadium has 30 entry gates. By midday, 14 more tickets sold. In the afternoon, two more matching sales hours tripled the total. By evening, six more matching sales hours made it seven times as large. Later, 72 more tickets sold. Finally, four more matching sales hours made the total five times as large. How many tickets were sold by the end of the day?

A charity had $230 in its fund, even though a dozen volunteers helped organize it. It spent $147 on event supplies. A small donation added $6. A larger donation added $45. A bank fee took $2. Half of the remaining fund was set aside for next year, and only that reserved half was tracked going forward. Finally, seven more matching donors joined, making that reserved amount eight times as large. How much money was in that reserved amount at the end?

Two rival orchards compared their apple harvests. Green Hill Orchard picked 83 crates of apples, even though the orchard has 40 acres of trees. A second picking added 58 more crates. A third picking added 65 more. Eight more matching orchards joined a co-op, making the total nine times as large. A late harvest added 74 more crates. Finally, eight more matching orchards joined again, making the total nine times as large, far ahead of the rival Sunset Orchard's 5,000 crates. How many crates of apples did Green Hill Orchard end up with?

Two rival gyms compared their equipment counts. Ironworks Gym had 226 dumbbells, even though the gym has 15 workout stations. A supplier recall removed 149 dumbbells. A quality check removed 4 more. A matching donation doubled the remaining count. A late shipment added 34 more. Finally, four more matching shipments made the total five times as large, leaving Ironworks Gym with far more than its rival, Peak Fitness, which only had 700 dumbbells. How many dumbbells did Ironworks Gym end up with?

Two sisters compared their savings for a trip, even though the trip costs a dozen different expenses to plan. Nour had 94 dollars saved. Half of it was set aside for souvenirs, and only that reserved half was tracked going forward. She earned 19 more dollars from chores. A birthday gift added 63 more dollars. That amount was then split evenly across 3 accounts, and only the travel account was tracked. Finally, 53 more dollars were added to the travel account, leaving her with more than her sister Lina. How much money did Nour have in the travel account at the end?

A factory produced 81 toy robots in the first hour, tracked over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of the shift. Two more matching hours tripled the total. Five more matching hours made it six times as large. Six more matching hours made it seven times as large. Finally, five more matching hours made it six times as large. How many toy robots did the factory produce in total?

A print shop had 140 flyers ready, even though the shop has a dozen printers. Six more matching print runs made the total seven times as large. Eight more matching runs made it nine times as large. Four more matching runs made it five times as large. Finally, 28 more flyers were added from a test print. How many flyers did the print shop end up with?

A vineyard had 185 crates of grapes, tracked over 120 minutes, or 2 hours, of the harvest, even though the vineyard has 30 acres. Eight more matching vineyards joined a co-op, making the total nine times as large. A shipment removed 1,197 crates for a spoiled batch. Four more matching vineyards joined, making the total five times as large. Finally, four more matching vineyards joined again, making it five times as large. How many crates of grapes did the co-op end up with?

In the morning, a parking garage had 126 cars parked, even though the garage has a dozen levels. By midday, 95 cars left for work, out of the 300 total spaces in the garage. In the afternoon, 18 more cars left for lunch. Later, 78 more cars arrived for a matinee show. By evening, 54 cars left as the show ended. How many cars were left in the garage by evening?

In the morning, two rival food banks compared donations. Riverside Food Bank had 205 cans donated. By midday, 7 more cans came in. In the afternoon, two more matching donation drives tripled the total. By evening, 78 more cans arrived from a school drive. Finally, 42 more cans came in from a late donor, leaving Riverside far ahead of the rival Lakeside Food Bank's 400 cans. How many cans did Riverside Food Bank end up with?

A bookstore had 65 novels on the clearance table, tracked over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of the morning rush, even though the store has a dozen genres. Eight more matching donations made the total nine times as large. Four more matching donations made it five times as large. A late donation added 45 more books. Another added 77 more. Finally, five more matching donations made the total six times as large. How many books were on the clearance table at the end?

In the morning, a warehouse had 194 crates stacked, even though the warehouse has 40 loading bays. By midday, two more matching shipments tripled the total. In the afternoon, five more matching shipments made it six times as large. By evening, eight more matching shipments made it nine times as large. Later, half of the crates were shipped to a sister warehouse, and only the remaining half stayed. Finally, 8,705 crates were sold off in a clearance sale. How many crates were left in the warehouse?

In the morning, a factory had 155 chairs assembled, even though the factory has a dozen assembly lines. By midday, three more matching production lines made the total four times as large. In the afternoon, four more matching lines made it five times as large. By evening, 33 more chairs came from a late run. Later, 1,666 chairs were shipped out for a big order. Finally, 45 more chairs were added from a returned shipment. How many chairs did the factory have by the end of the day?

Two rival trading card collectors compared totals. Zeke had 13 cards, even though the shop carries 60 different sets. Two more matching trades tripled his total. He won 6 more cards in a game. He lost 7 cards in a bad trade. A friend gave him 11 more cards. Seven more matching trades made his total eight times as large. Finally, he won 71 more cards in a tournament, ending up with more than his rival Cole. How many cards did Zeke end up with?
